The graph above is generated by the function $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(Bx).$ Find the value of $B.$
question.worked_solution:
In order to find the value of $B,$ we first need to find the period of the function.

From the graph, we can see that function makes $3$ complete cycles on the interval $[0,2\pi ].$ So, the period is $\frac{2\pi }{3}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14254788/assets/c17d8cbd806e89fbb2b1157d7096b5092949c37c7da12c9f55d4269a313458bf.png)

We know that for a function $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(Bx),$ the horizontal scaling factor is $\frac{1}{B},$ and the period is multiplied by the scaling factor:

$$
\text{period}=2\pi \cdot \frac{1}{B}
$$

For our particular function, the period is $\frac{2\pi }{3},$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\pi }{3} & =2\pi \cdot \frac{1}{B} \\ \frac{2\pi }{3} & =\frac{2\pi }{B} \\ B & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
